decisions.rationale: 'congenital hemolytic anemia' is a family of multiple specific anemias (e.g., G6PD deficiency and other inherited hemolytic anemias), so it is a Disease Class rather than one specific disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Disease Class vs Specific Disease

decisions.rationale: 'chronic nonspherocytic hemolytic anemia' groups several distinct anemias under one umbrella term, so it is a family of diseases and fits Disease Class.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Disease Class vs Specific Disease; Examples 11 (grey-area terms as Disease Class)

decisions.rationale: 'hemolytic anemia' used generically, without a single defined form, refers to a broad family of anemias, so it is a Disease Class.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Disease Class vs Specific Disease

decisions.rationale: 'G6PD deficiency' is a single, specifically defined enzymopathy with one definition and no further subcategorization in the text, so it is a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Specific Disease mentions; Examples 6 (C7 deficiency as Specific Disease)

decisions.rationale: 'hemolytic crisis' names a defined acute clinical episode of hemolysis that is a disease-state mention rather than a general term; it is annotated as a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Specific Disease mentions; What NOT to Annotate 4 (general terms) does not apply as it is a defined clinical condition

decisions.rationale: 'upper respiratory infection' is a family of multiple specific infections (e.g., pharyngitis, sinusitis, common cold), so it is a Disease Class.

'Infection-induced hemolysis' primarily denotes a biological process (hemolysis) triggered by infection; the disease-name tokens are not a standalone disease mention, and biological processes are excluded.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 5: references to biological processes

decisions.rationale: 'chronic hemolytic anemia' refers to a broad group of chronic anemias caused by hemolysis rather than one specific disease, so it is a Disease Class.
